# Fixture provenance

Every file under `tests/fixtures/` is **hand-authored** and contains **no real
saved-place data**. Place names, addresses, coordinates, and Google feature ids are
invented. Only the *structure* — column headers, JSON property names, directory
layout, byte encodings — mirrors a real Google Takeout export.

This is enforced by `tests/test_privacy_guard.py`, which fails if a fixture file is
not listed here. Real personal data lives in `data/`, which is gitignored.

Deliberately not generated by a redaction script over the real export: such a
script is exactly the kind of code whose bug leaks private data.

## takeout_min — the happy path

| File | What it exercises |
|---|---|
| `Takeout/Saved/Test Diner List.csv` | Two placeable rows; one non-Google URL that is an article, not a place |
| `Takeout/Saved/Test Favourites.csv` | Shares "Fictional Diner" with the list above (dedupe + membership union); ends with a blank line, as 2 of 35 real lists do |
| `Takeout/Maps (your places)/Saved Places.json` | One US place with coordinates, one foreign place (out-of-region flagging), one `[0,0]` entry with no `location` block (the real export's failure mode) |

## takeout_edge — encoding and malformed input

| File | What it exercises |
|---|---|
| `Takeout/Saved/Bom List.csv` | UTF-8 **with BOM** + CRLF + emoji/accented name. An unstripped BOM corrupts the first header key and silently loses the Title column |
| `Takeout/Saved/Utf16 List.csv` | UTF-16LE with BOM |
| `Takeout/Saved/Empty List.csv` | Header only — must yield zero entries, not an error |
| `Takeout/Saved/Messy List.csv` | A row with no URL; a row with a blank title |

## Notes from the real export (structure only, no data)

- Every real CSV has the header `Title,Note,URL,Tags,Comment` and is UTF-8 without
  a BOM. The BOM and UTF-16 fixtures are defensive: this machine has produced a
  UTF-16LE file before (`README.md`), so the reader must tolerate it.
- Real CSV URLs are `/maps/place/<Name>/data=!4m2!3m1!1s0x…:0x…`. The hex pair is a
  **feature id**, not a coordinate. No real URL contains extractable coordinates.
- `[0,0]` coordinates mean "absent", not a location in the Gulf of Guinea.
